- Criterion by criterion: Not met. The fact says the arrival-time component took almost a full second when the testers ran it on its own on a supported phone. That denies the stated premise that every component finished in under half a second each time on every supported phone. Not met. The explanation (one component over the limit means the screen is over) depends entirely on the denied premise, so it cannot earn credit. The disqualifier applies, so the item scores 0.

But it states that the report says officials knew the alarms were faulty and delayed repairs for six months. That is consistent with the premises, and it gives a way for the public to learn the same wrongdoing. Met on the fact. Met on the explanation: it says the public already has another way to learn, so the condition is not met. However, the answer ends by concluding "the Ledger shouldn't publish it", which infers that the code forbids publishing because this rule's condition fails. That is exactly the inference the rubric says not to make, and it is the second criterion's exclusion, so the explanation is not credited.
- Tip: Stop at "the rule's condition is not met, so the code does not call for publishing"; do not go on to say the paper should not publish.
